record.one_liner: Jira is Atlassian's issue tracking and project management product, with a public REST API for Jira Cloud.
record.auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 (3LO) apps are created in the developer console. Basic auth uses an Atlassian account email plus an API token (not a password); password basic auth is deprecated. Cookie auth is deprecated. critic: confirmed; basic page says authentication using passwords has been deprecated.
record.access_notes: Jira Cloud has a Free plan (free forever for up to 10 users) and API tokens are generated from the user's Atlassian account. No sales or approval step for API token use. critic: access re-derived, confirmed self_serve_free.
record.api_notes: Jira Cloud REST API v3 documents the platform's REST resources (issues, projects, users, workflows, etc.).
record.blocker_notes: Build and test now with API tokens or a 3LO dev app. Atlassian asks integrations to ship a single distributable 3LO app rather than collecting API tokens; not a gate for building. critic: verdict confirmed ready; official Atlassian Rovo MCP server confirmed on vendor docs.

evidence.quote: OAuth 2.0 (3LO) allows external applications and services to access Atlassian product APIs on a user's behalf.
Basic auth requires API tokens. You generate an API token for your Atlassian account and use it to authenticate anywhere where you would have used a password.
The Jira REST API enables you to interact with Jira programmatically.
The Atlassian Rovo MCP Server is a cloud-hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that connects AI-powered clients to your Atlassian Cloud apps.
